newsitem.title: JAPAN: McCartney birth certificate sold at Tokyo auction.
newsitem.headline: McCartney birth certificate sold at Tokyo auction.

text.p: The original birth certificate of Sir Paul McCartney was sold for 10.35 million yen ($84,146) in Tokyo on Saturday at the biggest-ever auction of memorabilia connected with the Beatles.
The price, which included a 15 percent auction house commission, was far above the pre-sale estimate of $13,000.

The sale of the certificate, the first of 300 Beatles items in a sale expected to last for four hours, had been denounced by McCartney who successfully stopped the auction house from selling the original lyrics to "Penny Lane," one of the Beatles' biggest hits.

The buyer of the certificate was an unidentified party in London. It was put up for sale by a California record collector. The birth certificate was originally sold by McCartney's stepmother after the death of his father.
The auction, by the firm Bonhams, was conducted simultaneously in London and Tokyo in order to tap into a growing interest in the Beatles in Japan.
Bonham officials expect the auction, which also includes the only guitar signed by all four musicians, to set world record prices for pop music souvenirs.
